hypotheses.justification: Implied by hy and hy' together with the junk-value conventions. If lam < 0, then 13/lam < 0, so hy' gives y < 0, which contradicts hy. If lam = 0, then 13/0 = 0, so 0 ≤ y ≤ 0 and y = 0. Also hinit becomes |H 0| ≤ N*C/0 = 0, so H 0 = 0. The left side is then |H 0|/(N*exp 0) = 0 and the right side is (…)/0 = 0, so 0 ≤ 0 holds. So we may first case-split on lam ≤ 0 and finish as above. In the lam > 0 case the existing proof applies unchanged.

Implied by hinit, hN and hlam: 0 ≤ |H 0| ≤ N*C/lam with N > 0 and lam > 0 gives C ≥ 0 (by div_nonneg_iff / pos_of_mul_pos-type reasoning, or nlinarith). The proof only uses C ≥ 0 implicitly in the final `positivity` call, so we add this derived fact first.

Implied by hsource, hy and hN: 0 ∈ Icc 0 y because hy gives 0 ≤ y, so 0 ≤ |g 0| ≤ N*M. With N > 0 this gives M ≥ 0. The proof uses hM in `mul_nonneg hN.le hM` (replace it with the derived N*M ≥ 0) and in `positivity` (supply the derived M ≥ 0).

Removable given hC and hM (but not together with them). If N = 0, the left side is |H y|/0 = 0, and the right side (C+13M)*exp 26/lam is ≥ 0 by hC, hM and hlam. If N < 0, then hsource at t = 0 (in Icc because of hy) gives 0 ≤ N*M, so M ≤ 0, and with hM, M = 0. Then g = 0 on Icc 0 y, so H y = H 0 by the same FTC step (heq). Also hinit gives |H 0| ≤ N*C/lam ≤ 0 because C ≥ 0, so H y = 0. The left side is 0 and the right side is ≥ 0. In the N > 0 case the existing proof applies.

Continuity of g is used only to make g interval-integrable for the FTC step. Instead we can bound |H y - H 0| ≤ N*M*y directly with Mathlib's mean value inequality `norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_deriv_le_segment'` (Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/MeanValue.lean). It needs `∀ x ∈ Icc 0 y, HasDerivWithinAt H (g x) (Icc 0 y) x`, which follows from hd via `HasDerivAt.hasDerivWithinAt`, and `∀ x ∈ Ico 0 y, ‖g x‖ ≤ N*M`, which follows from hsource. Applied at x = y this gives |H y - H 0| ≤ N*M*(y - 0), and the rest of the proof (the hvalue calc and hfactor) is unchanged.
